MY LEAF STUDIO

Make a Leaf Creature

Turn your rubbings into wings, scales, fur or feathers.

Look, then try.

Look at your rubbings and squint: a jagged rubbing might be a dragon's spiky back, a round one an owl's body, a long skinny one a cat's tail. Ask a grown-up to help cut out your favourite rubbings with safety scissors. Arrange the pieces on a fresh sheet without gluing first, moving them around until your creature appears. Then glue it down and add eyes, legs or a home with crayons. Your creature can be real or impossible: a leaf lion, a leaf spaceship, a leaf monster who loves salad.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

An adult helps with scissors when cutting out rubbings. Collect fallen leaves from the ground, or pick with permission, and brush off dirt and insects. Wash hands after handling leaves. Nothing you find outside goes in your mouth.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

Plan my creature

Draw your creature idea first. Which rubbing will be the body? The head? The tail?

ACTIVITY 2

Build it

Cut, arrange and glue your rubbings. Then draw the extra details with crayons.

ACTIVITY 3

Tell its story

Every creature has a story. What does yours eat? What does it do all day?

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

Cutting, arranging and combining shapes builds spatial thinking and fine motor control. Inventing a creature from textures also grows imagination and storytelling.
